subject: SOC2: log inventory + on-demand bundle packaging for GreenClinic
messages:
From: Jake Miller <jake.miller@greenclinic.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 evidence request — log inventory & on-demand bundle for GreenClinic

Hi Hannah,

We're in the middle of a SOC 2 readiness sprint and need a concrete plan for obtaining admin activity and audit logs from Redwood for our evidence bundle. Specifically GreenClinic audit requires: 

- An itemized inventory of what is logged (auth events, admin actions, policy changes, key rotation, model deployments, API requests with metadata).
- Retention policy by log class and where those logs live today (hosted API vs dedicated vs private).
- On-demand bulk export options (formats, compression, checksums, timezone normalization).
- Sampling/aggregation behavior (are some events sampled or aggregated after X days?).
- Chain-of-custody / manifest details (signed manifest, checksums, custody transfers).
- Expected timelines to produce a full per-account bundle for a 90-day window and for a 1-year window.

We'd like to know whether you can deliver the bundle to our secure SFTP or provide pre-signed S3 URLs, and what the secure transfer options are (encryption in transit / at rest, PGP).

Can you confirm what you can provide and an approximate lead time? Our auditor target date for ingest is 2026-06-07, so ideally we'd need handoff a week prior.

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Miller
Security Lead, GreenClinic Health
security@greenclinic.com

Hi Jake / team — here is the concrete inventory and export options from infra's side. TL;DR: we can produce full per-account admin activity bundles for both 90d and 1y windows; delivery options include encrypted S3 presigned URLs or SFTP with PGP; typical lead time 3-5 business days for 90d, 7-10 for 1y depending on warm archival retrieval.

What we log (per-account / operator-focused):
- Authentication events: successful and failed logins (timestamp, username, IP, auth method, MFA flag).
- Token and API key lifecycle: create/rotate/revoke events (actor, key id, timestamp).
- Role & permission changes: role grants/revokes, group membership changes.
- Admin console actions: user invites, password resets, MFA enforcement toggles.
- Model serving operations: model deployments, version pinning, rollback events, config changes (replica count, batching).
- Job and schedule events: batch job starts/stops/failures (job id, triggered_by).
- Configuration changes: network policy changes, private endpoint toggles, KMS/HSM key bindings.
- System alerts & operator escalations: operator acknowledgements and incident tags.

Retention & storage tiers (current defaults):
- Hosted API (default): event metadata retained 90 days in hot store, 1 year in cold archive (queryable via export request).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): hot store 365 days for operator events, archives configurable (enterprise customers often set 3+ years).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention varies by customer-managed config; we provide export tooling but archives are customer operated.

Export formats & packaging:
- Primary exports: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) or compressed CSV (CSV.GZ). We also support Parquet for large archives.
- Compression: gzip (.gz) or zstd (.zst) on request.
- Manifest: each bundle includes a manifest.json with file list, start/end timestamps, per-file SHA256 checksums, and a signed manifest token (internal RSA signature for chain-of-custody).
- Timezone: logs are normalized to UTC in the bundle; we include original timezone offsets in individual records where available.
- Sampling/Aggregation: we do not sample admin/operator events. High-volume request logs (non-admin API traffic) may be subject to rollup after 30 days; these are documented and we can provide raw if required for audit with additional runtime cost.

Chain of custody & verifiability:
- Bundles include: manifest.json (with SHA256s), a signed manifest signature file (manifest.sig), and a custody_transfer.txt that records the S3 presigned URLs or SFTP handoff details and the operator who exported the package.
- We can run a secondary HMAC (customer-provided secret) over the manifest for customers that require dual-control verification.

Delivery options & security:
- Preferred: encrypted S3 presigned URLs (KMS-encrypted at rest). We will encrypt artifacts server-side and provide presigned GETs valid for 72 hours by default.
- Alternate: SFTP push to customer host; we will provide .pgp-encrypted archive (you must provide public PGP key).
- Transfer integrity: SHA256 checksums and manifest.sig included. We can also provide GPG detached signatures on request.

Lead times & cost notes:
- 90-day bundle: 3 business days (no additional cost for SOC2 evidence requests within standard support).
- 1-year bundle: 7–10 business days (may require archive warm-up; cost depends on retrieval volume).

Attachments in this thread: redwood_admin_log_schema.csv (field map), admin_activity_manifest.json.gz (sample manifest), audit_export_playbook_v1.pdf (packaging & transfer playbook).

Let us know: 1) whether you need raw payloads, 2) SFTP or S3 preference, and 3) which exact start/end timestamps (UTC).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Infra Engineer — Exports
Redwood Inference
